title: Quasi-coherent sheaves on prestacks
summary: The functor-of-points theory of quasi-coherent sheaves: QCoh(X) as the limit of module infinity-categories over the affine points of a prestack, for classical, animated and connective E-infinity test rings over Z, with the coherent module functor and module theory of connective algebras, flat hyperdescent without finiteness hypotheses, invariance under fpqc sheafification, affine pushforward with base change, the comparison with quasi-coherent derived sheaves of every Mathlib scheme, the t-structure and perfect and almost perfect objects, quotients by group prestacks over a base and by discrete groups, classical quotient stacks, and compact generation and perfect stacks. It imports and extends PrismaticCohomologyPartII 4.0 (classical QCohPrestack), LanglandsParameterStacks 1.7 (animated faithfully flat descent) and HabiroCohomologyFoundations 1.27-1.28 (lattice quotients).

targets.name: Prestack.TestRings
targets.statement: The three infinity-categories of test rings CRing (nerve of CommRingCat), AnRing (AnimAlg_Z) and CAlg^cn = CAlg(D(Z)_{>=0}), linked by iota : CRing -> AnRing (discrete animated rings) and theta : AnRing -> CAlg^cn; homotopy groups pi_n A of a test ring, pi_0 A an ordinary commutative ring.

api.name: theta_preservesColimits

api.name: theta_preservesFiniteProducts

api.name: pushout_tor

api.name: initial_final

tests.name: zero_ring

hypotheses: A is a connective commutative algebra of D(Z)

locator.where: Proposition 7.1.1.13, p. 1202; Definition 7.2.2.10, Proposition 7.2.2.13 and Theorem 7.2.2.15, pp. 1240-1241

api.name: flat_tExact
api.statement: Extension along a flat map is t-exact; along a faithfully flat map it is moreover conservative.

api.name: flat_stable
api.statement: Flat and faithfully flat maps are stable under composition and base change; iota and theta preserve and reflect them.

api.name: lazard
api.statement: A connective module is flat iff it is a filtered colimit of finite free modules.

api.name: flat_classical

targets.name: Prestack.Mod.Perf

api.name: aperf_closure

api.name: baseChange_stable

api.name: discrete_comparison

tests.name: Z_plus_Z3

tests.name: dual_numbers

tests.name: infinite_poly

tests.name: truncation_unstable

targets.name: Prestack.limit_adjointable
targets.statement: (a) A natural transformation of diagrams K -> Cat_infty-hat, K (u+1)-small, with componentwise right adjoints and right adjointable naturality squares has a componentwise right adjoint on limits, and the projection squares are right adjointable. (b) Dualizable (invertible) objects of a limit of symmetric monoidal infinity-categories are those with dualizable (invertible) images; the invertible half from the dualizable half, invertible = dualizable with evaluation an equivalence, and equivalences in a limit being detected componentwise. (c) Descent criterion: an augmented cosimplicial infinity-category satisfying Beck-Chevalley is a limit diagram iff C^{-1} -> C^0 is comonadic.
hypotheses: K is a (u+1)-small infinity-category, so that limits over K exist in Cat_infty-hat
for (c), each coface square is right adjointable

locator.where: Corollary 4.7.4.18, p. 699; Proposition 4.6.1.11 and Remark 4.6.1.12, p. 620; Theorem 4.7.5.2 and Corollary 4.7.5.3, pp. 704-705; Proposition 5.2.2.36, p. 835; SAG Remark 2.9.5.5, p. 283; HTT Propositions 2.4.1.5 and 3.1.2.1, PDF pp. 134 and 169-170

api.name: adjointable_limit

api.name: dualizable_limit
api.statement: Dualizable objects of a limit are detected componentwise; so are invertible ones, an object being invertible exactly when it is dualizable with evaluation an equivalence, and equivalences in a limit being detected componentwise.

api.name: descent_criterion
api.statement: Beck-Chevalley plus comonadicity of C^{-1} -> C^0 gives C^{-1} = lim C^.

tests.name: empty_diagram
tests.statement: The empty limit is the zero category; its object is dualizable and invertible.

tests.name: product_dualizable

tests.name: compact_not_componentwise

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh
targets.statement: QCoh : PreStk_T^op -> CAlg(Cat_infty-hat), the right Kan extension of Spec A |-> Mod_A along Spec, QCoh(X) = lim over Pts(X) of Mod_A; evaluation eta^*, pullback f^*, structure sheaf O_X. In the classical context QCoh is PrismaticCohomologyPartII 4.0 QCohPrestack (same limit of R |-> D_infty(R) with derived base change, identified through 1.2 classical values), with its eval, pullback, specEquiv and unit_eval; the statement here extends it to AnRing and CAlg^cn.
hypotheses: T is one of the three contexts

Cat_infty-hat is the infinity-category of (u+1)-small infinity-categories (EnhancedDerivedSheaves Cat_infty, E0.5, in the universe u+1); every Mod_A, every Pts(X) and every QCoh(X) is (u+1)-small, while PreStk_T is only locally (u+1)-small and is not an object of Cat_infty-hat

tests.statement: QCoh(empty) is the zero category; a colimit formula would give the empty infinity-category.

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.formal
targets.statement: QCoh carries (u+1)-small colimits of prestacks to limits; QCoh(X) is stable with u-small colimits computed pointwise; f^* preserves u-small colimits and is symmetric monoidal; tensor is pointwise and preserves colimits in each variable; equivalences and zero objects are detected pointwise, vanishing of maps is not (except on affines, through the initial point); QCoh(X) is presentable for X a u-small colimit of affines; in CRing the homotopy category of QCoh(Spec R) is DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R) with shift and triangles. In the classical context these are PrismaticCohomologyPartII 4.0 limitOfColimit, isEquiv_iff_eval and homotopyCategory_spec, extended here to the animated and E-infinity contexts.
hypotheses: X is a prestack on one of the three contexts
for presentability, X is a u-small colimit of affines

api.name: colimits_to_limits
api.statement: QCoh(colim X_i) = lim QCoh(X_i) for every (u+1)-small colimit of prestacks.

api.name: stable_colimits

api.name: pointwise_tensor

api.name: conservative
api.statement: A map is an equivalence, and an object is zero, iff all evaluations are (1.5); vanishing of maps is not detected pointwise.

api.name: homotopyCategory

tests.name: Zp_tensor

tests.name: vanishing_not_pointwise

For u = iota or theta iota the source side is PrismaticCohomologyPartII 4.0 QCohPrestack(X).

targets.name: Prestack.ofScheme
targets.statement: The classical prestack h_X of a Mathlib scheme X, R |-> Hom(Spec R, X), and the classical prestack X^natural of a SchemeAndStackFoundations stack in groupoids, by straightening the nerve of its Grothendieck construction over affines; the fppf topology on CRing^op (finite families with faithfully flat and finitely presented product), fppf sheaves and L_fppf, identified with Mathlib's fppf topology on affine schemes; h is fully faithful; compatibility with 2-fibre products and of stackification with L_fppf.
hypotheses: X a Mathlib scheme, or a StackInGroupoids of SchemeAndStackFoundations section 1.18

locator.where: Proposition 2.1.1.3 (PDF p. 75) and Proposition 1.2.5.1 (PDF p. 53)

api.name: fppf_topology
api.statement: An fppf cover of R is a finite family {R -> S_i} with R -> prod S_i faithfully flat and finitely presented; Phi' is the class of Spec S -> Spec R with R -> S faithfully flat and finitely presented. Phi' contains the isomorphisms and is stable under composition, base change and finite products (finite presentation being Zariski-local on Spec(R x R')); finite coproducts of CRing^op are universal and disjoint; so HypercompletenessAndCoherence 9.3.2 gives the topology whose covering sieves contain an fppf cover, and its sheaves are the fppf sheaves, the functors CRing -> S-hat preserving finite products with Cech descent along Phi' (9.4.1, SAG A.3.2.1, A.3.3.1). L_fppf is the left adjoint of their inclusion, the accessible localization of EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2.7 in the universe u+1.

api.name: fppf_mathlib_comparison
api.statement: The covering sieves of Mathlib's fppfTopology are those containing an fppfPrecoverage covering family (Precoverage.mem_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderComposition). An fppf cover is such a family; conversely a covering family {X_i -> Spec R} of fppfPrecoverage is quasi-compact (fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage), so finitely many affine opens Spec S_j of the X_i cover Spec R and {R -> S_j} is an fppf cover refining it.

api.name: h_fullyFaithful
api.statement: h is fully faithful and h_{Spec R} = Spec R.

api.name: value_nerve
api.statement: X^natural(R) is the nerve of the groupoid X(Spec R), a Kan complex.

api.name: fibreProducts
api.statement: (-)^natural carries 2-fibre products to fibre products of prestacks.

api.name: stackification
api.statement: (-)^natural, formed by the same construction for every groupoid-valued pseudofunctor F on schemes, carries fppf stackification (SchemeAndStackFoundations 1.18 Stack.stackification) to L_fppf: the map L_fppf(F^natural) -> (stackification F)^natural induced by the unit is an equivalence. Its target is an fppf sheaf (Stack.isStack_stackification on the covers of affines given by fppf covers of rings). It is a monomorphism: over each pair of points of F^natural, the diagonal is the map from the Isom presheaf in F to that in the stackification, its fppf sheafification (Stack.stackification_isom_sheafify), inverted by the left exact, colimit-preserving L_fppf (universal colimits, InfinityTopoi 3.3.2). It is an effective epimorphism: objects of the stackification are fppf-locally in the image (Stack.stackification_locally_essSurj) and InfinityTopoi 9.2.3 applies to the fppf topology. Hence an equivalence (InfinityTopoi 7.3.4).

tests.name: spec_case
tests.statement: h_{Spec R} = Spec R; restriction to fields is not faithful on Spec k[e].

tests.name: BZ2_real
tests.statement: For G = Z/2, (BG)^natural(R-real) has two components and pi_1 = Z/2 at the trivial torsor; over R x R it has pi_1 = (Z/2)^2.

tests.name: pi0_loses
tests.statement: Replacing groupoids by isomorphism classes gives a point on strictly henselian local rings and loses pi_1 = G(R).

tests.name: Zp_not_fppf
tests.statement: Z -> Z[1/p] x Z_p is faithfully flat but not an fppf cover: finitely generated Z-algebras are countable and its quotient Z_p is not; so Phi' is strictly smaller than the faithfully flat maps.

tests.name: infinite_mathlib_family
tests.statement: {Spec Z[1/n] -> Spec Z : n >= 2} is an infinite fppfPrecoverage covering family; its subfamily n = 2, 3 is an fppf cover refining it (Z[1/2] x Z[1/3] faithfully flat and finitely presented), while n = 2 alone misses (2).

targets.name: Prestack.fpqcTopology
targets.statement: The fpqc topology on T^op by finite families with faithfully flat product, flat hypercovers (latching maps faithfully flat), fpqc sheaves and hypercomplete sheaves (finite products and Cech descent, respectively flat hyperdescent), valued in spaces or in any infinity-category C with (u+1)-small limits, identified with the sheaves and hypercomplete sheaves of the topology generated by the faithfully flat maps, and the (hyper)sheafification L, with its universal property for functors preserving (u+1)-small limits.
hypotheses: T is one of the three contexts

api.name: sheaf_criteria
api.statement: The faithfully flat maps Phi of T^op satisfy (a)-(d) of HypercompletenessAndCoherence 9.3.2 (equivalences and composites; base change; finite products of test rings are the coproducts of T^op and are stable; C = (C (x)_{AxB} A) x (C (x)_{AxB} B) for A x B -> C, and 0 (x)_A C = 0) and (e) of 9.4.1 (A (x)_{AxB} B = 0, so coproducts are disjoint). So 9.3.2 gives the topology whose covering sieves contain an fpqc cover; its C-valued sheaves are the C-valued fpqc sheaves (9.4.1, SAG A.3.3.1); flat hypercovers are the Phi-hypercoverings (11.5.1, SAG D.6.1.4), and the hypercomplete C-valued sheaves (11.5.2) are the hypercomplete C-valued fpqc sheaves (11.5.3, SAG A.5.7.2).

api.name: stability
api.statement: Covers and flat hypercovers are stable under base change and composition; iota and theta carry covers to covers, Cech nerves to Cech nerves and flat hypercovers to flat hypercovers. For theta, which preserves colimits and homotopy groups, this is immediate. For iota, the latching object L_n is reached from A by adjoining the proper subsets of [n] one at a time in order of size, each step a pushout along a lower latching map L_m -> A_m (m < n), which is faithfully flat, and flat pushouts agree in CRing and AnRing; so by induction on n the ordinary and derived latching objects and maps agree.

api.name: mathlib_comparison
api.statement: In CRing a family is a cover iff the Spec family is an fpqcPrecoverage covering.

api.name: sheafification
api.statement: L is left exact and preserves colimits.

api.name: fppf_to_fpqc
api.statement: In CRing, Phi' (2.5) is contained in Phi, so every (hypercomplete) fpqc sheaf on CRing^op is an fppf sheaf and every map of classical prestacks inverted by L_fppf is inverted by L and by the hypersheafification (Map(f, F) = Map(L_fppf f, F) for an fpqc sheaf F); the affine form of Mathlib's fppfTopology_le_fpqcTopology. Z -> Z[1/p] x Z_p is in Phi and not in Phi'.

api.name: universal_property

api.name: geometric_quotient
api.statement: For every G the atlas X -> [X/G] is an fpqc surjection: X -> |G^{x_S .} x_S X| is an effective epimorphism of PreStk_T (its Cech nerve is the effective action groupoid, InfinityTopoi 7.1.1), its hypersheafification is one of hypercomplete fpqc sheaves (InfinityTopoi 7.4.1), so every point Spec R -> [X/G] lifts to X after an fpqc cover {R -> R_i} (3.1, local lifting), along which the base change of L X -> [X/G] is L(G x_S Spec R_i) -> Spec R_i (effectivity, L left exact, L Spec R_i = Spec R_i by 3.2), the hypersheafification of a base change of G -> S split by the unit; when X and G x_S Spec R_i are hypercomplete fpqc sheaves (for instance X affine and G affine over S, 3.2, 4.1), L X = X and this is the base change of the atlas itself, the projection G x_S Spec R_i -> Spec R_i; for the constant group Z/2 it is not (test realization_diagonal). If S and X are affine and G is affine over S, [X/G] has affine diagonal: X x X -> [X/G] x [X/G] is an fpqc surjection, the base change of the diagonal along it is X x_{[X/G]} X = G x_S X -> X x X (effectivity, L left exact, affines fixed by L, 3.2), a map of affines, and affineness is local on the target (4.1); so the atlas is affine. If moreover G is flat over S, the atlas is flat (its base change along a point becomes flat after R -> prod R_i, and flatness descends along faithfully flat maps, 6.1), so [X/G] is geometric (6.2); flatness of G gives the flatness of the atlas, not its surjectivity.

api.name: trivial

G acting on itself by translation has bar construction the Cech nerve of G -> S split by e, realization S and [G/G] = L S.

The atlas S -> BG is affine and an fpqc surjection, its base change along itself being G -> S split by the unit, but that base change is not flat, so this atlas does not make BG geometric. For G = G_m the base change Spec Z[t, t^-1] -> Spec Z is free and BG_m is geometric.

tests.name: realization_diagonal
tests.statement: For Gamma = Z/2 the fibre of the diagonal of the constant prestack B Gamma over the base points at R is Spec R + Spec R (prestack coproduct); for R = Z its value at Z x Z has 2 points, while an affine Y has Y(Z x Z) = Y(Z) x Y(Z), 4 points; so the realization has no affine diagonal. Its hypersheafification is also the quotient by L Gamma = Spec(Z x Z), affine over Spec Z, and the fibre becomes Spec(R x R), affine. Accordingly the base change of the atlas Spec Z -> [Spec Z/Gamma] along itself is L Gamma = Spec(Z x Z), with 4 points at Z x Z (the idempotents of Z x Z), not the constant prestack Gamma, with 2: X is a sheaf, Gamma x Spec Z is not.

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.realizationEquiv

For the action of the dual group on the framed derived cocycle functor in the animated context the limit is the enhanced QCoh of LanglandsParameterStacks 1.8 (the same bar construction), which this extends to every action of a group prestack. Its perfect objects (6.3) are its chartwise dualizable objects, as LanglandsParameterStacks 1.8 defines Perf on its stacks: an object of the limit is dualizable iff each term is (1.5), and each term is the pullback of the term on X along the map induced by a vertex [0] -> [n]; so it is perfect iff its term on X is dualizable in QCoh(X).
hypotheses: S a prestack; G a group prestack over S acting on X over S

targets.name: Prestack.IsPerfectStack.permanence
targets.statement: (a) Affine over perfect is perfect (classical: flat affine over perfect). (b) Classical: if f : Y -> X is flat and representable by qcqs schemes (5.4(b)), X is perfect, and a set {L_i} of invertible objects of QCoh(Y) restricts on every base change Y_eta to an ample family of invertible modules (Stacks tag 0FXR), then Y is perfect; one ample invertible object is the one-member case. (c) Animated, E-infinity: every morphism between perfect stacks has perfect base change along every point of the target; classical: every morphism representable by qcqs schemes with affine diagonal (every base change along a point a qcqs scheme with affine diagonal) has perfect base change along every point, with no flatness and no perfectness of source or target. (d) Animated, E-infinity: for perfect X_1, X_2 over Y with affine diagonal, X_1 x_Y X_2 is perfect (Y final: X_1 x X_2). Classical: if X_2 is perfect and X_1 -> Y is flat affine or of the kind in (b), then X_1 x_Y X_2 is perfect.

(b) classical context; f flat and representable by qcqs schemes; X perfect; {L_i} invertible objects of QCoh(Y) forming an ample family on every base change Y_eta along a point of X
(c) animated and E-infinity: source and target perfect; classical: the morphism representable by qcqs schemes with affine diagonal
(d) animated and E-infinity: X_1, X_2 perfect, Y with affine diagonal; classical: X_2 perfect, X_1 -> Y flat affine or of the kind in (b)

api.name: BGLn
api.statement: BGL_n is perfect in characteristic zero. It has affine diagonal (7.4 with X = Spec k), and QCoh((BGL_n)^natural) is QCoh of the geometric stack [Spec k/GL_n] of 7.1, its fpqc hypersheafification (7.4(a), 3.3(a), 7.2; t-structures agree as connectivity is fpqc-local, 6.1), whose t-structure is left and right complete (6.2(b)). Complete reducibility (ReductiveGroups Layer 6) and local finiteness (Layer 1, heart of 7.4(c)) make the heart semisimple, so Ext^i vanishes in it for i > 0; by 7.4(d), for the quasi-compact [Spec k/GL_n] with affine diagonal, pi_0 Map(O, M[i]) = Ext^i(O, M) in the heart for M in the heart. So RGamma = q_* carries the heart to the heart; it is left t-exact (right adjoint of the t-exact q^*), right t-exact on bounded objects by induction and on connective M by left completeness (pi_0 RGamma(tau_{<=m} M) constant in m, no lim^1); so pi_0 Map(V[i], M) = Hom(V, pi_i M) for finite-dimensional V in degree zero and all i (a statement about pi_0 only); these V are compact and dualizable and generate; the compact = dualizable objects are their stable retract-closed span, the objects with finitely many nonzero pi_i, each finite-dimensional, including shifts such as O[1].

tests.name: twist_not_product
tests.statement: k = Q, G = Z/2, X = G with translation and L = O, so [X/G] = Spec Q; along the torsor P = Spec Q(i) over Q the base change is P x^G G = Spec Q(i), with no Q-point, whereas X x Spec Q = Spec Q + Spec Q has two: Zariski gluing would give the wrong scheme.

tests.name: twist_descent_datum
tests.statement: Same G and P, X = P^1_Q with G acting through diag(1,-1) on Q^2 and L = O(1): the descent datum on Q(i)^2 is conjugation composed with diag(1,-1), invariants Q e1 + Q i e2, so P x^G X = P(Q e1 + Q i e2) = P^1_Q with O(1) ample; conjugation alone would fix Q^2 and forget the torsor.

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.notCompact_charP
targets.statement: For G = Z/p over F_p, O_{BG} is dualizable and not compact, so BG is not perfect; more generally on B Gamma x Spec k for a finite group Gamma and a field k of characteristic p dividing |Gamma|, O is dualizable and not compact. Route: an element of order p (Cauchy) generates C; V = Coind_C^Gamma k has H^i(Gamma; V) = H^i(C; k) = k for all i >= 0 (Shapiro and the cyclic computation), and pi_0 Map(O, V[i]) = H^i(Gamma; V); then pi_0 Map(O, (+)_i V[i]) = prod_i k, not the sum.
hypotheses: Gamma finite, k a field of characteristic p dividing |Gamma|

locator.where: Introduction, p. 1 (non-tame stacks: the structure sheaf is perfect and not compact); HNR Theorem 1.1, pp. 1-2, and section 4, p. 9 (compact generation fails for poorly stabilized stacks, a class not containing B(Z/p))

api.name: mapping_groupCohomology
api.statement: For a k-linear representation V of a finite group Gamma (Mathlib Rep k Gamma) in the heart of Fun(B Gamma, Mod_k), pi_0 Map(O, V[i]) = H^i(Gamma; V) (Mathlib groupCohomology), Map(O, V[i]) being Omega^infty of V^{h Gamma}[i] (2.2) and the cohomology of V^{h Gamma} being group cohomology (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:presentability.3 continuousDerivedInvariants).

api.name: coinduced_witness
api.statement: With g of order p (exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card), C = <g> and V = Coind_C^Gamma k (Rep.coind), H^i(Gamma; V) = H^i(C; k) = k for every i >= 0 by groupCohomology.coindIso and Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.groupCohomologyIsoEven/Odd (maps g - 1 = 0 and norm p = 0).

api.name: product_vs_sum
api.statement: In Fun(B Gamma, Mod_k), (+)_{i>=0} V[i] = prod_{i>=0} V[i], so pi_0 Map(O, (+)_i V[i]) = prod_i k, while compactness of O would give the sum (+)_i k.

tests.name: trivial_group
tests.statement: For trivial Gamma, O is compact: H^i = 0 for i > 0, and there is no element of order p.

tests.name: Zp_Fp
tests.statement: H^i(Z/p; F_p) = F_p for all i >= 0, so the comparison sum -> product is not surjective.

tests.name: S3_F3
tests.statement: For Gamma = S_3 over F_3, H^1(S_3; F_3) = Hom(S_3, F_3) = 0 and H^2(S_3; F_3) = 0 (the C_2 = S_3/C_3 action on H^2(C_3; F_3) = F_3 is -1), but V = Coind_{C_3}^{S_3} F_3, two-dimensional, has H^i(S_3; V) = F_3 for every i, so the comparison (+)_i F_3 -> prod_i F_3 is not surjective.

tests.name: Zp_Q
tests.statement: Over Q, H^i = 0 for i > 0 and O is compact (8.4).

tests.name: regular_rep_compact
tests.statement: Compact generation is not what fails: Fun(B Gamma, Mod_k) is generated by the compact regular representation k[Gamma], Map(k[Gamma], M) being Omega^infty of the underlying k-module of M; for Gamma = Z/p, k = F_p, pi_0 Map(k[Gamma], (+)_{i>=0} O[i]) = k = (+)_i pi_0 Map(k[Gamma], O[i]), whereas pi_0 Map(O, (+)_i O[i]) = prod_i F_p.

gaps.title: Chevalley's theorem: GL_n/H is quasi-projective
gaps.detail: For a field k, an affine group scheme H of finite type over k and a closed immersion H -> GL_n, the fppf quotient GL_n/H is represented by a quasi-projective k-scheme admitting a GL_n-equivariant immersion into the projectivization of a finite-dimensional representation, so that O(1) is a GL_n-linearized ample line bundle. Used in the proof of BZFN Corollary 3.22 (p. 24) to make BG perfect from BGL_n.
gaps.needs: A statement that the fppf quotient of GL_n by a closed subgroup scheme of finite type over a field is a quasi-projective scheme with a GL_n-equivariant immersion into the projectivization of a finite-dimensional representation.

gaps.title: Contracted products of quasi-projective schemes with a linearized ample bundle are quasi-projective schemes
gaps.detail: For a field k, an affine group scheme G of finite type over k, a quasi-projective k-scheme X with a G-action and a G-linearized ample invertible module L, and a G-torsor P over an affine k-scheme Spec R, the contracted product of SchemeAndStackFoundations 1.16 is represented by a scheme, flat and quasi-projective over R, with the descended L ample. One route: trivialize P over a faithfully flat finitely presented R -> R', where the twist is X_R' with the relatively ample pullback of L and the linearization gives a compatible descent datum; descent of quasi-compact schemes with a compatible relatively ample invertible module along a faithfully flat quasi-compact map is effective with the descended module relatively ample (SGA1, Expose VIII, Proposition 7.8, p. 174). Needed by 8.4 because G-torsors need not be Zariski-locally trivial (Z/2 over Q, P = Spec Q(i)).
gaps.needs: A statement that for a field k, an affine group scheme G of finite type over k, a quasi-projective k-scheme X with a G-action and a G-linearized ample invertible module L, and a G-torsor P over an affine k-scheme Spec R, the contracted product P x^G X is represented by a scheme, flat and quasi-projective over R, on which the module descended from L is ample.
